description.p: A coding agent with a GPU-rendered UI and a headless core: long-term memory with a review inbox, worktree tabs, subagents, skills, MCP, and permission modes that keep every mutating action behind a card you approve.

The flatpak runs commands through your host environment, so your toolchains (rust, node, go, python) work as they do outside the sandbox; every action is gated by the permission mode you choose, and full access costs a confirmation card.

The status column: the open session's state lives beside the transcript — what the agent is working on, its next step, the memory it remembered, the files it touched, the memory entries its work depends on, questions from other sessions, and pending corrections. Collapses to a rail; every section renders only when it has something to say.
A grounded run shows a riding line on the latest turn: what the work rests on, cited by entry id.

Memory you can trust: a superseded entry rides search results pointing at its replacement, writing through the tool shapes the store exactly like writing through the ops path, recall fires when the agent reads a memory file, and a repo map gives navigation a ranked view of the workspace.
Projects: named groups in the sidebar to file conversations under, one project per chat, filed by hand.

Memory you can trust longer: entries cite the files they came from and are flagged when those files change, a superseded entry records its replacement, and correcting an entry flags the ones that rested on it for you to keep or archive.
An AGENTS.md in a subdirectory applies when the agent works under it. A worker's approval request now reaches only the chat that started it.
A UX pass: the sidebar drives parallel chats (no tab bar), a Stop button for running turns, settings that save as you go, and a header for each conversation.

Security hardening: web fetches ask first, a repository's own settings can only tighten yours, writes refuse raced symlinks, reads refuse special and oversized files, and gertie run --yes refuses uncommitted work unless --allow-dirty is given.
Deb, rpm, and flatpak packaging; the Orchard listing.
The first release: the whole contract, from the memory review inbox to the mode menu.
